excerpt: Walk the yard at the real hour, count the chairs in actual shade, and put water and fans out before anyone sits. This is a seating plan, not a decorative sail.

title: A Backyard Wedding with a Pool: Cover It, Fence It, or Keep a Watch
short: A Backyard Wedding with a Pool
excerpt: Treat the pool as water, not decor: close it with a cover or a fence, or assign a sober adult, and light the edge after dusk.

title: Wedding Peach Cobbler in 9x13 Pans: A Warm Tray Dessert for a Crowd
excerpt: Peaches and a biscuit topping, baked in 9x13 pans until the fruit bubbles and the top is browned. Two pans serve about 24; four, about 48. Serve warm.

title: Wedding Tres Leches in 9x13 Pans: A Soaked Cake You Make Ahead and Keep Cold
excerpt: A sponge baked in 9x13 pans, soaked with three milks, topped with whipped cream, and kept cold. Two pans serve about 24; four, about 48.

title: Wedding Potato Salad for a Crowd: A Make-Ahead Cold Side, Kept Chilled
excerpt: Boiled potatoes, a mayonnaise dressing with mustard, celery and onion, made ahead and kept cold. About 6 pounds of potatoes serve 24 as a side; about 12 pounds, 48.

title: Bugs at an Outdoor Wedding: Standing Water, Candles, and a Station People Can Choose
excerpt: Empty standing water, be honest about citronella, cover the food, and set a labeled wipe station no one is required to use. This is a yard plan, not a decorating problem.

title: A Backyard Wedding Aisle: A Path People Can Actually Walk
excerpt: Give the aisle a width, a clear start, and a runner only if you can keep it down. Grass is enough when it is even and dry; soft ground wants boards or a heavier cloth you can stake.

title: A Shuttle for a Backyard Wedding: A Loop to a House That Has No Parking Lot
excerpt: One pickup point, a sign, a driver who is not in the wedding party, and a last ride after dark. This is how guests get to a house without filling the street.

title: A Day-of Coordinator for a Backyard Wedding: One Person, a Binder, and Authority
excerpt: Give the day to one person who is not in the wedding party, with a printed timeline, a working kit, and the right to make small decisions without finding you.

title: Leftover Wedding Food: Pack It, Label It, and Keep It Safe
excerpt: Decide who takes what before the last toast, pack leftovers while they are still safe to pack, and label every lid. Keep hot food hot or cool it quickly; keep cold food cold.

title: Wedding Lemon Bars in 9x13 Pans: A Cool Tray Dessert You Cut Cold
excerpt: A shortbread crust and a lemon filling, baked in 9x13 pans, chilled thoroughly, and cut into squares. Two pans serve about 24 generous squares; four, about 48.

title: Wedding Coleslaw for a Crowd: A Vinegar Slaw That Can Sit
excerpt: Shredded cabbage and carrot in a cider-vinegar dressing, made ahead and kept cool. About 4 pounds of cabbage serve 24 as a side; about 8 pounds, 48. It is not another mayonnaise salad.

title: Wedding Baked Beans for a Crowd: A Thick Pot, Held Hot
excerpt: Canned beans baked with onion, molasses, and mustard until the pot is thick. About 4 quarts serve 24 as a side; about 8 quarts, 48. Hold at or above 140°F, and label a meatless pot if you make one.

title: A Morning Backyard Wedding: Dew, Sun, and a Day That Ends While It Is Light
excerpt: Walk the yard at the real morning hour, dry the chairs, put the ceremony out of the sun, and tell guests when the day actually ends. This is a clock, not a brunch menu.

title: Cleanup After a Backyard Wedding: Trash, a Named Person, and a House You Can Use
excerpt: Put lidded cans out, empty them during the event, name who stays after the last car, and leave the hosts a house. This is not leftover food, and it is not a hope that someone will start the dishwasher.

title: A Backyard Wedding Welcome Table: Programs, a Card Box, and a Sign People Can Read
excerpt: Put one table at the actual entrance, with a readable sign, a card box that closes, and programs only if you need them. It is not a second reception, and it is not a welcome bag.

title: Backyard Wedding Photography: Light, a Family List, and What to Tell the Photographer
excerpt: Walk the yard at the real hour, pick two or three portrait spots, and give someone other than the couple a short family-photo list. This is a location plan, not a tutorial for photographers.

title: A Unity Candle at an Outdoor Wedding: A Flame, a Shield, and a Backup
excerpt: If you want a unity candle in a yard, test it at the real hour, in a hurricane or a weighted holder, and have a backup line if the wick will not stay lit. Or choose a ritual that does not need a flame.

title: Wedding Brownies in 9x13 Pans: A Cool Tray of Squares You Cut After They Cool
excerpt: A cocoa brownie batter, baked in 9x13 pans until just set, cooled completely, and cut into squares. Two pans serve about 24 generous squares; four, about 48. They are not a cookie table.

title: Wedding Bread Pudding in 9x13 Pans: A Warm Custard Tray You Can Assemble Ahead
excerpt: Cubed slightly stale bread soaked in a simple custard, baked in 9x13 pans until the center is set, and served warm. Two pans serve about 24; four, about 48. It is not banana pudding, and it is not cobbler.

title: Wedding Chicken Salad for a Crowd: A Cold Bowl, Kept Cold
excerpt: Cooked chicken, chopped and dressed with mayonnaise, lemon, and celery, then thoroughly chilled. About 4 pounds of cooked chicken serve 24 as a generous side or filling; about 8 pounds, 48. Keep it cold.

title: Winter Wedding Centerpieces Without Flowers: Pine, Cones, and Candlelight That Behave
excerpt: Winter wedding centerpieces on a budget, no florist needed: evergreen runners, pine cones, berries, and candlelight in glass. Five formulas, per-table counts, fresh-greenery tips, and a flame plan.

title: A Zero-Waste Backyard Wedding: Real Dishes, Honest Bins, and One Bag on Sunday
excerpt: How to plan a zero-waste (or honestly low-waste) backyard wedding: rent real dishes, use cloth, check what your town composts, label the bins, and pack leftovers before the last toast.

title: Kids at a Backyard Wedding: A Table, a Kit, a Quiet Corner, and a Grown-Up in Charge
excerpt: Kids at a backyard wedding without the meltdown: a clear kids policy, a yard hazard walk, a kids' table, one activity per stretch, ear protection, a nap room, and a sitter.

title: Wedding Cupcakes for a Crowd: How Many to Bake, How to Freeze, and a Vanilla Recipe
excerpt: DIY wedding cupcakes: about one to one and a half per guest, baked in batches of 24, frozen ahead, frosted the day before. Includes a vanilla buttermilk cupcake and buttercream recipe.

title: Wedding Sangria for a Crowd: A Winter Red Batch You Mix the Night Before
excerpt: Big-batch wedding sangria: red wine, brandy, orange, apple, and cranberry, chilled overnight and topped with sparkling water. About 24 glasses per batch, with an alcohol-free version.

title: Wedding Charcuterie Cups: A Grazing Table You Can Hold in One Hand
excerpt: Charcuterie cups for a wedding cocktail hour: about one per guest, prepped the day before, assembled a few hours ahead, and served cold in waves. Recipe for 24 or 48 cups.

title: How Much Champagne for a Wedding Toast (and How to Pour It Without a Bar Staff)
excerpt: How much champagne for a wedding toast: about one bottle per 6 to 8 drinking guests, plus 10%. How to chill it, pre-pour trays, offer sparkling cider, and batch a cranberry-rosemary toast.

title: A Homemade Wedding Sheet Cake: Servings, Two Thin Layers, and a White Almond Recipe
excerpt: How to make a wedding sheet cake at home: a two-layer half sheet serves about 48, layers bake and freeze ahead, and it rides flat in a box. Includes a white almond cake and buttercream recipe.

title: Glazed Ham for a Wedding Crowd: How Much to Buy, How to Warm It, and a Brown Sugar Glaze
excerpt: How much ham for a wedding: about 1/2 pound of bone-in spiral ham per guest as the main. Warm fully cooked hams to 140°F, glaze, hold, and carve, with a brown sugar–Dijon recipe for 24 or 48.

title: A Wedding Donut Wall: How Many to Order, How to Build It, and a Baked Donut Recipe
excerpt: Plan a wedding donut wall: about one donut per guest with cake, two if it's the dessert. Build, buy, or rent the wall, load it an hour ahead, and bake vanilla donuts for 24 or 48.

title: A Barn Wedding on a Budget: What the Fee Covers, What to Spend On, and What to Skip
short: A Barn Wedding on a Budget
excerpt: Barn wedding ideas on a budget: read what the barn fee includes, book off-season, spend on warm light instead of florals, plan for heat, dust, and doors, and skip the burlap-on-everything look.

title: Dried Flowers for a Wedding: Bouquets, Centerpieces, and How to Keep Them From Shedding
excerpt: Dried flowers for a wedding: buy mixed bundles or dry your own, build a bouquet in an afternoon, make centerpieces that last all weekend, mix in fresh stems, and keep pampas from shedding.
